parts.label: a
hints: Sum the 5 values and divide by 5 to determine the mean.
The median is the 3rd value in the ordered list of 5 values.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the mean of the five observations:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{4 + 6 + 6 + 8 + 11}{5} = \frac{35}{5} = 7$$

Identify the median from the ordered values:
$$\text{Position} = \frac{5 + 1}{2} = 3^{\text{rd}}\text{ value} \implies \text{Median} = 6$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Add all readings to calculate the arithmetic mean:
$$\sum x = 4 + 6 + 6 + 8 + 11 = 35,\quad \bar{x} = \frac{35}{5} = 7$$

Locate the middle value in the sorted dataset:
$$\text{Ordered set: } \{4, 6, 6, 8, 11\} \implies \text{Median} = 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sum the 5 values and divide by 5: (4 + 6 + 6 + 8 + 11) / 5.
Obtain mean = 7 and median = 6.

parts.label: a
hints: Consider how the sum and arithmetic mean are pulled upward by extreme scores.
The median depends only on rank order and remains stable.

walkthrough.text:
Select the appropriate measure of central tendency:
$$\text{Selected measure: Median}$$

State the statistical rationale regarding the extreme value 73:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{165}{5} = 33,\quad \text{Median} = 24$$
$$\text{The extreme score 73 distorts the mean upward, whereas the median is unaffected.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the preferred central metric for skewed data:
$$\text{Measure: Median}$$

Explain the sensitivity of the mean versus robustness of the median:
$$\text{The outlier 73 inflates the mean to 33, while the median 24 represents typical scores accurately.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State median as the preferred measure of central tendency.
Explain that the extreme value 73 inflates the mean, while the median remains unaffected.

parts.label: a
hints: A complete key must include a sample stem and leaf, an equals sign, the numerical value, and the unit.
Count to the 5th value in order out of the 9 observations to find the median.

walkthrough.text:

$$\text{Key: } 2 \mid 1 = 21\text{ years}$$

Locate the 5th observation in the ordered diagram:
$$\text{Rank} = \frac{9 + 1}{2} = 5^{\text{th}}\text{ item} \implies \text{Median} = 27\text{ years}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate a clear key specifying stem, leaf, and units:
$$\text{Key: } 1 \mid 8 = 18\text{ years}$$

Find the middle age of the 9 individuals:
$$\text{Ages: } 18, 21, 24, 24, 27, 30, 32, 35, 41 \implies \text{Median} = 27$$

ai_rubric.observable: Provide a correct key with units, for example 2 | 1 = 21 years.
Identify median = 27.

parts.label: a
hints: Consider which display retains every individual raw score.
A box plot condenses data into five summary statistics, losing original values.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the fundamental information preserved in a stem-and-leaf diagram:
$$\text{The stem-and-leaf diagram keeps and shows every individual data value.}$$

Contrast this with the summary nature of a box plot:
$$\text{A box plot summarizes data into five points, so individual scores cannot be retrieved.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compare the data fidelity of both charts:
$$\text{Stem-and-leaf retains all raw values: } x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{50}$$

State the key analytical advantage:
$$\text{Individual frequencies and exact values remain visible in the stem-and-leaf diagram.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Mention that the stem-and-leaf diagram retains original individual data values.
Contrast with box plots which summarize data into five values and lose individual scores.

parts.label: a
hints: Recall that frequency density is defined as class frequency divided by class width.
Class width is the difference between upper and lower boundaries: $12 - 10$ and $16 - 12$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate class widths for both intervals:
$$w_1 = 12 - 10 = 2,\quad w_2 = 16 - 12 = 4$$

Compute frequency densities:
$$\text{FD}_1 = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5,\quad \text{FD}_2 = \frac{15}{4} = 3.75$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the width of each continuous class:
$$w_1 = 2\text{ cm},\quad w_2 = 4\text{ cm}$$

Apply the standard frequency density formula:
$$\text{Frequency Density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class Width}}$$
$$\text{FD}_1 = \frac{5}{2} = 2.5,\quad \text{FD}_2 = \frac{15}{4} = 3.75$$

ai_rubric.observable: Apply frequency density = frequency / class width for at least one interval.
Obtain correct frequency densities 2.5 and 3.75.

parts.label: a
hints: Compare medians for typical values: Group Y is 31 and Group X is 28.
Compare interquartile ranges ($Q_3 - Q_1$) for the spread of the middle 50%.

walkthrough.text:
Compare typical running times using medians:
$$\text{Median}(Y) = 31 > \text{Median}(X) = 28 \implies \text{Group Y has higher typical running time.}$$

Compare middle 50% spread using interquartile ranges:
$$\text{IQR}(X) = 34 - 25 = 9,\quad \text{IQR}(Y) = 36 - 22 = 14$$
$$\text{Group X has a less variable middle 50\% than Group Y.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Quote both medians to establish the difference in centre:
$$\text{Median}(Y) = 31\text{ min} > \text{Median}(X) = 28\text{ min}$$

Quote both IQRs to establish the difference in middle spread:
$$\text{IQR}(X) = 9\text{ min},\quad \text{IQR}(Y) = 14\text{ min} \implies \text{Group X is more consistent in the middle 50\%}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State that Group Y has a higher typical time quoting medians 31 and 28.
State that Group X has less spread in the middle 50% quoting IQRs 9 and 14.

parts.label: a
hints: There are 12 ordered values. The median is the average of the 6th and 7th values.
Find lower quartile $Q_1$ from the lower 6 values and upper quartile $Q_3$ from the upper 6 values.

walkthrough.text:
Find the median as the midpoint of the 6th and 7th values:
$$\text{Values: } 18\text{ and } 18 \implies \text{Median} = \frac{18 + 18}{2} = 18\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Locate the middle pair of the 12 ordered observations:
$$\text{Median} = \frac{18 + 18}{2} = 18$$

ai_rubric.observable: State median = 18.
Calculate IQR = 21 - 15.5 = 5.5.

parts.label: b
hints: Identify the specific outlier in the dataset.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the extreme value in the dataset:

State the statistical consequence on the mean:

Explain that the mean is disproportionately increased and not representative.

parts.label: a
hints: The modal class is the interval with the highest frequency.
Cumulative frequencies allow you to locate the 20th and 21st observations.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the modal class by greatest frequency:
$$\text{Highest frequency is } 14 \implies \text{Modal class is } 20 - 29$$

Calculate cumulative frequencies to find median position:
$$\text{Cumulative frequencies: } 6, 20, 32, 40$$
$$\text{The 20.5}^{\text{th}}\text{ item falls into } 20 - 29\text{ or } 30 - 39\text{ (accepted } 20 - 29\text{ as 20th item)}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Locate the interval with maximum frequency count:
$$\text{Frequency } 14 \implies \text{Class } 20 - 29$$

Determine the interval containing the median rank:
$$\frac{40}{2} = 20^{\text{th}}\text{ value} \implies \text{Interval } 20 - 29$$

ai_rubric.observable: State modal class = 20 - 29.
Identify median class interval as 20 - 29 (or 30 - 39 based on (n+1)/2).

parts.label: b
hints: Find the midpoint of each class interval: 14.5, 24.5, 34.5, 44.5.
Multiply each midpoint by its frequency, sum $\sum f x$, and divide by 40.

walkthrough.text:
Find the midpoints of the class intervals:
$$x_1 = 14.5,\quad x_2 = 24.5,\quad x_3 = 34.5,\quad x_4 = 44.5$$

Divide by total frequency 40 to find the estimated mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{1200}{40} = 30$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up midpoints representing each score class:
$$x = [14.5, 24.5, 34.5, 44.5]$$

Multiply frequencies by class midpoints:
$$\sum f x = (6 \times 14.5) + (14 \times 24.5) + (12 \times 34.5) + (8 \times 44.5) = 1200$$

Evaluate estimated mean:
$$\bar{x} = \frac{1200}{40} = 30$$

ai_rubric.observable: Determine correct midpoints 14.5, 24.5, 34.5, 44.5.
Evaluate sum f*x = 1200 and divide by 40.
Obtain mean = 30.

parts.label: a
hints: For $n = 15$, the median is the 8th value.
The lower quartile is the 4th value and upper quartile is the 12th value.
Subtract $Q_1$ from $Q_3$ to find the interquartile range.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the 8th value for the median:
$$\text{Position} = \frac{15 + 1}{2} = 8^{\text{th}}\text{ value} \implies \text{Median} = 57\%$$

Identify quartiles and compute IQR:
$$Q_1 = 4^{\text{th}}\text{ value} = 51\%,\quad Q_3 = 12^{\text{th}}\text{ value} = 65\%$$
$$\text{IQR} = 65 - 51 = 14\%$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Locate the middle element of the 15 ordered scores:
$$\text{Median} = 8^{\text{th}}\text{ value} = 57$$

Determine the lower quartile and upper quartile ranks:
$$Q_1 = 4^{\text{th}}\text{ score} = 51,\quad Q_3 = 12^{\text{th}}\text{ score} = 65$$
$$\text{IQR} = 65 - 51 = 14$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtain median = 57%.
Obtain IQR = 65 - 51 = 14%.

parts.label: b
hints: Compute the step: $1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 1.5 \times 14 = 21$.
Calculate the lower threshold $Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$ and upper threshold $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR}$.
Compare the minimum score (42) and maximum score (76) to these thresholds.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the boundary step $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$:
$$1.5 \times 14 = 21$$

Calculate lower and upper fences:
$$\text{Lower threshold} = Q_1 - 21 = 51 - 21 = 30\%$$
$$\text{Upper threshold} = Q_3 + 21 = 65 + 21 = 86\%$$

Check minimum and maximum values against thresholds:
$$\text{Min} = 42 > 30,\quad \text{Max} = 76 < 86$$
$$\text{Conclusion: There are no outliers.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate the 1.5 IQR product:
$$1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 1.5(14) = 21$$

Establish lower and upper cutoff boundaries:
$$\text{Lower fence} = 51 - 21 = 30,\quad \text{Upper fence} = 65 + 21 = 86$$

Compare all observations to the fences:
$$\text{Since all values lie within }[30, 86]\text{, there are no outliers.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate 1.5 * IQR = 21.
Establish lower threshold 30 and upper threshold 86.
Conclude correctly that there are no outliers as 42 >= 30 and 76 <= 86.

parts.label: a
hints: Divide each class frequency by its class width: $\text{FD} = f / w$.
Check units and decimals for each class.

walkthrough.text:
Find the class widths for each interval:
$$w_1 = 30 - 20 = 10,\quad w_2 = 35 - 30 = 5,\quad w_3 = 45 - 35 = 10,\quad w_4 = 60 - 45 = 15$$

Calculate frequency densities for intervals 1 and 2:
$$\text{FD}_1 = \frac{12}{10} = 1.2,\quad \text{FD}_2 = \frac{15}{5} = 3.0$$

Calculate frequency densities for intervals 3 and 4:
$$\text{FD}_3 = \frac{13}{10} = 1.3,\quad \text{FD}_4 = \frac{10}{15} = \frac{2}{3} \approx 0.667$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the width of each continuous interval:
$$w = [10, 5, 10, 15]$$

Apply frequency density = frequency / width to first two classes:
$$\text{FD}_1 = \frac{12}{10} = 1.2,\quad \text{FD}_2 = \frac{15}{5} = 3.0$$

Apply to final two classes:
$$\text{FD}_3 = \frac{13}{10} = 1.3,\quad \text{FD}_4 = \frac{10}{15} = \frac{2}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify correct class widths: 10, 5, 10, 15.
Apply frequency density formula frequency / width.
Obtain correct frequency densities: 1.2, 3.0, 1.3, and 2/3 (or 0.667).

parts.label: b
hints: For class $30 \le x < 35$, width 5 corresponds to $2\text{ cm}$, so scale for width is $2 / 5 = 0.4\text{ cm per unit}$.
For height, frequency density is $3.0$ which corresponds to $9\text{ cm}$, so height scale is $9 / 3 = 3\text{ cm per unit of FD}$.
Apply these two linear scales to the class $45 \le x < 60$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the width scaling factor and the bar width for $45 \le x < 60$:
$$\text{Scale for width} = \frac{2\text{ cm}}{5\text{ units}} = 0.4\text{ cm/unit}$$
$$\text{Width} = 15 \times 0.4 = 6.0\text{ cm}$$

Find the height scaling factor:
$$\text{Scale for height} = \frac{9\text{ cm}}{3.0\text{ FD}} = 3.0\text{ cm per unit FD}$$

Compute the bar height for $\text{FD} = \frac{2}{3}$:
$$\text{Height} = \frac{2}{3} \times 3.0 = 2.0\text{ cm}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the scale on the horizontal axis (class width to cm):
$$\text{Width scale} = \frac{2}{5}\text{ cm per unit} \implies \text{Width} = 15 \times \frac{2}{5} = 6\text{ cm}$$

Determine the scale on the vertical axis (frequency density to cm):
$$\text{Height scale} = \frac{9\text{ cm}}{3.0} = 3\text{ cm per unit FD}$$

Calculate the height for the class with width 15 and frequency 10:
$$\text{FD} = \frac{10}{15} = \frac{2}{3} \implies \text{Height} = \frac{2}{3} \times 3 = 2\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Use proportional scaling for width: 15 * (2/5).
Obtain width = 6 cm.
Obtain height = 2 cm from height scale 3 cm per unit FD.

parts.label: a
hints: Compare medians: Alpha is 85 miles and Beta is 95 miles.
Calculate overall range: $\text{Range}(\text{Alpha}) = 160 - 40 = 120$ miles, $\text{Range}(\text{Beta}) = 155 - 50 = 105$ miles.
State the conclusions in context with numerical evidence.

walkthrough.text:
Compare medians with context:
$$\text{Median}(\text{Beta}) = 95\text{ miles} > \text{Median}(\text{Alpha}) = 85\text{ miles}$$
$$\text{Beta has higher typical daily mileage.}$$

Calculate overall ranges:
$$\text{Range}(\text{Alpha}) = 160 - 40 = 120\text{ miles},\quad \text{Range}(\text{Beta}) = 155 - 50 = 105\text{ miles}$$

Compare spread with context:
$$\text{Alpha has greater overall variation in daily mileage than Beta.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compare central tendencies using median values:
$$\text{Median: Beta (95) is greater than Alpha (85)}$$

Compute ranges for overall spread:
$$\text{Alpha: } 160 - 40 = 120,\quad \text{Beta: } 155 - 50 = 105$$

Synthesize comparison in context:
$$\text{Beta has higher typical mileage, while Alpha shows greater overall spread.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: State that Beta has higher typical daily mileage quoting medians 95 and 85 miles.
Calculate range for both companies: Alpha = 120, Beta = 105.
State that Alpha has greater overall spread quoting ranges 120 and 105 miles.

parts.label: b
hints: Calculate interquartile ranges: $\text{IQR}(\text{Alpha}) = 110 - 65 = 45$, $\text{IQR}(\text{Beta}) = 115 - 80 = 35$.
State which company has less variability in the middle 50%.
For the advantage, mention direct visual comparison of medians and IQRs on a common scale.

walkthrough.text:
Compute interquartile range for each company:
$$\text{IQR}(\text{Alpha}) = 110 - 65 = 45\text{ miles},\quad \text{IQR}(\text{Beta}) = 115 - 80 = 35\text{ miles}$$

Compare middle 50% spread:
$$\text{Beta has less spread in the middle 50\% of journeys than Alpha (35 vs 45).}$$

State the advantage of paired box plots:
$$\text{Paired plots on one scale make it easy to visually compare medians, IQRs, and skewness directly.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate the width of the central box for each distribution:
$$\text{IQR}(\text{Alpha}) = 45,\quad \text{IQR}(\text{Beta}) = 35$$

Interpret the comparison of middle 50% consistency:
$$\text{Beta has a more compact middle 50\% of daily mileages.}$$

Explain why parallel box plots are effective:
$$\text{Aligned plots allow immediate visual comparison of central tendency and dispersion.}$$

State that Beta has a more consistent middle 50% of mileage.
State that paired plots on a single scale facilitate direct visual comparison of medians and spreads.

parts.label: a
hints: For 11 ordered values, $Q_1$ is the 3rd value and $Q_3$ is the 9th value.
Calculate $Q_1 = 76$, $Q_3 = 90$, and $\text{IQR} = 90 - 76 = 14$.
Compute the upper threshold $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 90 + 21 = 111\text{ kg}$.
Compare 115 to 111 and state the conclusion.

walkthrough.text:
Find quartiles and IQR for the rugby team:
$$Q_1 = 3^{\text{rd}}\text{ value} = 76\text{ kg},\quad Q_3 = 9^{\text{th}}\text{ value} = 90\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{IQR} = 90 - 76 = 14\text{ kg}$$

Calculate the upper boundary fence:
$$\text{Upper fence} = Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 90 + 1.5(14) = 90 + 21 = 111\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{Since } 115 > 111\text{, the mass } 115\text{ kg is an outlier.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine the lower and upper quartile values from ranks 3 and 9:
$$Q_1 = 76,\quad Q_3 = 90 \implies \text{IQR} = 14$$

Apply the standard 1.5 IQR boundary rule:
$$\text{Threshold} = 90 + 1.5(14) = 111$$
$$\text{As } 115\text{ exceeds } 111\text{, it is officially classified as an outlier.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate IQR = 90 - 76 = 14 and upper fence 90 + 1.5(14) = 111.
Conclude that 115 is an outlier because 115 > 111.

parts.label: b
hints: Leaves on the left for Rowers must increase going to the left away from the stem.
Leaves on the right for Rugby must increase going to the right away from the stem.
Provide a complete dual key identifying both teams and including units (kg).

walkthrough.text:
Set up stems from 6 to 11 and place leaves in ascending order from the stem:
$$\begin{array}{rcccl} \text{Rowers} & & \text{Stem} & & \text{Rugby} \\ \hline & & 6 & & 8 \\ 8\quad 5\quad 2 & & 7 & & 4\quad 6\quad 9 \\ 8\quad 5\quad 4\quad 2\quad 1\quad 0 & & 8 & & 2\quad 5\quad 7\quad 8 \\ 5\quad 1 & & 9 & & 0\quad 2 \\ & & 10 & & \\ & & 11 & & 5 \end{array}$$

Provide a complete key representing both teams with units:
$$\text{Key: } 8 \mid 7 \mid 4 \text{ means } 78\text{ kg for Rowers and } 74\text{ kg for Rugby}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Organize data into ascending stems with leaves ordered outward from the stem:
$$\text{Stems } 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11$$
$$\text{Rowers on LHS, Rugby on RHS with consistent spacing}$$

Write a dual-sided key with context:
$$\text{Key: } 2 \mid 8 \mid 5\text{ represents } 82\text{ kg for Rowers and } 85\text{ kg for Rugby}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Include correct stems 6 to 11 (or 6 to 9 and 11) with proper alignment.
Provide correct ordered leaves on both sides (Rowers ascending leftwards, Rugby ascending rightwards).
Include a correct complete key identifying both teams and including kg.

parts.label: c
hints: For Rowers: 11 values, median is the 6th value = 82 kg.
Lower quartile is 3rd value = 78 kg, upper quartile is 9th value = 88 kg, so IQR = 10 kg.
Compare medians: Rugby (85 kg) > Rowers (82 kg).
Compare spread: Rugby IQR (14 kg) > Rowers IQR (10 kg), meaning Rowers have less spread in the middle 50%.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate median and IQR for Rowers:
$$\text{Median} = 6^{\text{th}}\text{ value} = 82\text{ kg}$$
$$Q_1 = 78\text{ kg},\quad Q_3 = 88\text{ kg} \implies \text{IQR} = 88 - 78 = 10\text{ kg}$$

Compare typical masses in context:
$$\text{Median}(\text{Rugby}) = 85\text{ kg} > \text{Median}(\text{Rowers}) = 82\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{The rugby team has a higher typical mass than the rowing crew.}$$

Compare dispersion in context:
$$\text{IQR}(\text{Rugby}) = 14\text{ kg} > \text{IQR}(\text{Rowers}) = 10\text{ kg}$$
$$\text{The masses of the rowers are less spread out in the middle 50\% than the rugby players.}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Extract 5-number statistics for the rowing crew:
$$\text{Median} = 82,\quad Q_1 = 78,\quad Q_3 = 88 \implies \text{IQR} = 10$$

Evaluate relative central location:
$$\text{Rugby players are heavier on average (median 85 kg vs 82 kg)}$$

Evaluate middle 50% consistency:
$$\text{Rowers have more uniform masses in the middle 50\% (IQR 10 kg vs 14 kg)}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Obtain Rowers median = 82 kg and IQR = 10 kg.
State that Rugby team has higher typical mass quoting medians 85 and 82 kg.
State that Rowers have less spread in the middle 50% quoting IQRs 10 and 14 kg.

parts.label: a
hints: Recall that frequency density is given by class frequency divided by class width.
Apply frequency density = frequency / class width for each of the five classes.
Verify all 5 calculated frequency densities carefully.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the class widths of all five intervals:
$$w_1 = 20,\quad w_2 = 10,\quad w_3 = 15,\quad w_4 = 15,\quad w_5 = 20$$

Compute frequency densities for the first three intervals:
$$\text{FD}_1 = \frac{10}{20} = 0.5,\quad \text{FD}_2 = \frac{15}{10} = 1.5,\quad \text{FD}_3 = \frac{30}{15} = 2.0$$

Compute frequency densities for the remaining two intervals:
$$\text{FD}_4 = \frac{18}{15} = 1.2,\quad \text{FD}_5 = \frac{12}{20} = 0.6$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Tabulate class intervals and respective widths:
$$w = [20, 10, 15, 15, 20]$$

Calculate frequency density as count per unit width:
$$\text{FD} = \frac{f}{w} \implies [0.5, 1.5, 2.0, 1.2, 0.6]$$

ai_rubric.observable: Find class widths: 20, 10, 15, 15, 20.
Apply frequency density = frequency / class width across intervals.
Obtain correct frequency densities: 0.5, 1.5, 2.0, 1.2, 0.6.

parts.label: b
hints: Calculate the area of the given bar: $\text{Area} = 5 \times 6 = 30\text{ cm}^2$.
In a histogram, area is directly proportional to frequency.
Class $20 \le t < 30$ has frequency 15, so find area per unit frequency: $30 / 15 = 2\text{ cm}^2$ per employee.
Multiply by total frequency 85 to find total area.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the area of the bar for $20 \le t < 30$:
$$\text{Area}_{20-30} = 5\text{ cm} \times 6\text{ cm} = 30\text{ cm}^2$$

Establish the proportionality constant between area and frequency:
$$\text{Frequency} = 15 \implies k = \frac{30\text{ cm}^2}{15\text{ employees}} = 2.0\text{ cm}^2\text{ per employee}$$

Multiply by total frequency 85:
$$\text{Total Area} = 85 \times 2.0 = 170\text{ cm}^2$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compute area of the specified reference bar:
$$\text{Area} = 5 \times 6 = 30\text{ cm}^2$$

Use the histogram property that area is proportional to frequency:
$$\frac{\text{Area}}{\text{Frequency}} = \frac{30}{15} = 2\text{ cm}^2\text{ per unit frequency}$$

Compute total histogram area:
$$\text{Total Area} = 85 \times 2 = 170\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Calculate area of given bar = 5 * 6 = 30 cm^2.
Use proportionality of area to frequency: 30 / 15 = 2 cm^2 per frequency.
Obtain total area = 170 cm^2.

parts.label: c
hints: Divide $\sum f x = 3385$ by 85 to find the mean.
Median position is $85 / 2 = 42.5$, check cumulative frequencies to locate the median class interval.

walkthrough.text:
Determine class midpoints:
$$x = [10,\; 25,\; 37.5,\; 52.5,\; 70]$$

Calculate total sum $\sum f x$ and estimated mean:
$$\sum f x = 10(10) + 15(25) + 30(37.5) + 18(52.5) + 12(70)$$
$$\sum f x = 100 + 375 + 1125 + 945 + 840 = 3385$$
$$\bar{t} = \frac{3385}{85} \approx 39.8\text{ minutes}$$

Identify median class interval from cumulative frequencies:
$$\text{Cumulative frequencies: } 10, 25, 55, 73, 85$$
$$\text{Position } 42.5^{\text{th}}\text{ lies in interval } 30 \le t < 45$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up products of class midpoints and frequencies:
$$\sum f x = 10(10) + 15(25) + 30(37.5) + 18(52.5) + 12(70) = 3385$$

Evaluate mean commute time:
$$\bar{t} = \frac{3385}{85} = 39.8235... \approx 39.8\text{ minutes}$$

Locate median class using cumulative frequency table:
$$\text{Median rank } 42.5 \implies \text{Class interval } 30 \le t < 45$$

ai_rubric.observable: Determine correct midpoints and calculate sum f*x = 3385.
Obtain mean = 39.8 minutes (or 3385/85).
Identify median class interval as 30 <= t < 45.
